correctness.rationale: The six-color partition follows by intersection of named-ground-set stars and the five-element remainder; both independent C++ and Python exhaustive 5-color searches construct exactly 57 triples and 498 disjointness edges and rule out 5-colorings by 122153 complete canonical branches. The independent verifier checks all six dihedral deletion-orbit witnesses and their transport to all 57 vertices. The group symmetry is checked directly, clique number is bounded by ten ground-set labels. No timeout/incomplete enumeration is accepted as proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper explicitly treats the cycle-plus-isolate case only asymptotically and conjecturally, not as a finite proven boundary, and does not give the six-orbit vertex-critical certificate. Schrijver 1978 establishes the corresponding chromatic/criticality result for single-cycle stable sets, a different 50-vertex graph. Relevant published-source and database searches found no exact 57-vertex statement. Authors report unspecified earlier computational tests, so unreported prior knowledge remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Arana et al. explicitly describe computational tests consistent with their conjecture but do not identify tested parameter instances; the first exact numerical case might have been verified privately or in unindexed supplementary work.
Not all archival full-text sources of Schrijver-type generalizations were inspected, and search coverage cannot establish absolute historical priority.
The exhaustive coloring obstruction relies on independently replayable, finite program execution; no externally certified unsatisfiability proof is supplied.

value.rationale: The graph is the first unresolved cycle-plus-isolate threshold instance for k=3 of an explicit 2026 conjecture: cycle length 9 immediately after the known exclusion at 8. The result proves exact tightness, stronger vertex criticality for every triple, and a natural 3-versus-6 clique/chromatic gap with six-orbit proof data. It resolves a motivated boundary rather than a random isolated computation; the full conjecture is not asserted.
